title: The Timeline revamp PR added IssueBulkUpdateDateEndpoint, which fetches issues by caller-supplied ids without filtering by the URL's workspace and project, so a member of any project can change start/target dates of any issue on the instance.

findings.explanation: All database queries use Django ORM with parameterized queries. The `issue_filters` function processes query params and `order_by_param` is passed to `order_issue_queryset` which presumably validates/allowlists ordering fields. No raw SQL or string interpolation into queries is visible in this diff.

In `IssueBulkUpdateDateEndpoint.post`, issues are fetched by `id__in=issue_ids` without verifying that those issues belong to the `project_id` or `workspace__slug` from the URL. A member of one project could potentially supply issue IDs from another project they don't have access to. The `IssueDetailEndpoint.get` filters by `workspace__slug=slug, project_id=project_id` so that one appears safe. The bulk update endpoint lacks the project/workspace scope filter on the initial fetch.

evidence.content:
issue_ids = [update["id"] for update in updates]

        issues = list(Issue.objects.filter(id__in=issue_ids))

findings.suggested_fix: Filter issues by both workspace slug and project_id when fetching: `Issue.objects.filter(id__in=issue_ids, project_id=project_id, workspace__slug=slug)` to ensure only issues belonging to the authorized project are updated.
